text:
Sam: Heads up — ran into ambiguity in the queue boundary semantics today. When batch windows cross tenant bursts, small-req tenants can starve long-req tenants. Need to clarify design before we ship the new batcher.
Elena: Can you paste a minimal repro and the config you used? cc @Priya since this touches admission/batching.
Sam: Repro sketch: two tenants A (many tiny requests) and B (few long requests). Batcher groups by arrival across tenants every 1s window, so tiny reqs fill the batch and B waits for next window -> 30% p95 spike in our sim. Config: `batch.window_ms=1000`, `max_batch_tokens=65536`.
Priya: Two clear options: (1) strict per-tenant subqueues (one queue per tenant) or (2) keep shared queue with weighted admission that reserves slots for long requests. Per-tenant solves fairness but causes fragmentation and more scheduling complexity.
Devin: Also: our frontdoor doesn't surface expected cost. If callers could pass a hint (est_tokens / priority), admission could make better packing decisions. i.e. `X-Expected-Tokens` and `X-Priority-Hint` headers.
Sam: +1 on hints. Also the prefix cache warmups create lots of tiny hits which skew the batcher. We should consider capping tiny requests per-tenant per-window or prioritizing cache-warmed requests lower.
Elena: Tradeoffs: per-tenant queues -> deterministic fairness and clear quota boundaries but higher memory and harder burst-smoothing. Shared weighted approach -> simpler resource usage but worst-case latency can be unbounded for some tenants.
Priya: My proposal: short-term add optional admission hints (`X-Expected-Tokens`, `X-Priority`) and a conservative default for missing hints. Medium-term: virtual subqueue abstraction in the batcher — subqueues per tenant when they exceed a threshold, otherwise collapse into shared queue.
infra-bot: Feature flag created: `ingress.admit_hints` and a gateway change ticket (GW-452) to passthrough headers to admission service.
Devin: Implementation idea: model virtual subqueues as lightweight token buckets backed by a shared pool; collapse them when unused to avoid slot explosion. Will draft micro-RFC with interface sketch + perf test plan.
Elena: :thumbsup: Add an e2e scenario that mixes tiny/long requests across N tenants and measures per-tenant p50/p95/p99 and collapse events.
Sam: I'll open the micro-RFC and include telemetry suggestions: `tenant.queued_bytes`, `tenant.queued_count`, `subqueue_collapse_events`, and `hint_mismatch_rate`.
Priya: Also remember billing implications — fragmentation may change our cost math and reserved-capacity accounting. We'll need a short note for finance/docs if we go per-tenant.
Devin: I'll post a draft RFC tomorrow morning and add a perf harness run. If folks want, we can sync Wed 10am to decide which path to take.
Elena: Sounds good. Thanks for catching this, Sam.
